patch.value: Preview and review destination changes for pending Slack events

Preview explicit alias-to-alias route transitions on the durable Slack outbox. The outbox remains the delivery engine; route configuration changes are separate from reliability, notification disclosure and standup digest policies.

No event silently targets both old and new destinations; already uncertain sends retain uncertainty; replay creates no duplicate queue entries; preview posts nothing; queued use of the new route requires a reviewed binding revision.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Overlap rechecked on 2026-10-28: pm-slack main 911d78a owns SQLite delivery, history recovery, coalescing and route explanations; no open destination-migration PR or issue exists. CLI public SDK declarations expose tracker transactions, status registries, history and complete reads, but no Slack route migration API. Standup main f1d1187 builds reports; observer main 7aba36e queues PM evidence notes; ops has no Slack routing transition. This feature reuses the durable outbox and its delivery proof, not another delivery engine or disclosure policy. Planned design: explicit aliases bind to credential-free existing configured routes; monotonic binding revision and exact queue-plan revision require review; preview uses the same evaluator as atomic apply; uncertainty and receipt identities survive. Plans cover only currently pending, proven-unsent owned receipts. Tracker records are observed through SDK complete/history reads and never rewritten.

Found and fixed coalesced-drain stale-route race by revalidating destination inside claim. First focused regressions passed 7/7; typecheck and docstring gate passed. Building 500-sequence model and exhaustive statement-boundary concurrency/crash tests next.

value.text: Final producer/preview agreement audit found two concrete boundary cases in the new feature: preview did not preflight revision-capacity exhaustion, and adding a target channel could emit a payload above the documented size cap that a later preview would reject. Moving capacity and mapped-payload validation into the shared evaluator, counting payloads in UTF-8 bytes, and adding exact-boundary regressions before the final gate. Current source and tracker heads passed their release gates; those results do not certify this correction.
